file_line: src/cMake/Model.cmake:5-30; src/CMakeLists.txt:95-140,305; src/contact_models.h (fallback specialization removed, was HEAD:contact_models.h:272)
summary: A default CMake configure generates a 4-entry contact-model whitelist (HERTZ x {TANGENTIAL_HISTORY,NO_HISTORY} x {SJKR,SJKR2} x EPSD2 x DEFAULT) with no COHESION_OFF/ROLLING_OFF entry. Now that the GranStyle<> fallback is gone, the default CMake binary rejects even 'model hertz tangential history'.
failure_scenario: A user builds with plain `cmake ../src && make`, and 19 of 23 shipped Tutorials_public decks abort at pair_style with 'not compiled into the static contact-model whitelist'. The same CMake configuration at HEAD runs 18 of 23, because HEAD still has the fallback.
recommendation: Make WRITE_WHITELIST always add the *_OFF entries (Make.sh does this: tangential/cohesion/rolling OFF are prepended). Better, have CMake take its list from a tracked whitelist file or from genAutoExamplesWhitelist.sh. Or restore the fallback behind an opt-in option such as LIGGGHTS_ALLOW_SLOW_FALLBACK. Add a CI job that runs every example deck on the CMake-default binary.

summary: Even with the curated 124-entry whitelist the branch was built with, the combination (HERTZ, TANGENTIAL_HISTORY, COHESION_OFF, ROLLING_OFF, SURFACE_MULTICONTACT) is missing. The shipped deck hydrogel_multicontact/in.hydrogel_multicontact ran at HEAD through the fallback and now hard-errors.
failure_scenario: Running examples/LIGGGHTS/Tutorials_public/hydrogel_multicontact/in.hydrogel_multicontact on the modified build aborts at pair_style. At baseline it ran, with an 'unoptimized version' warning.
recommendation: Add the combination to the whitelist. Regenerate the whitelist from all shipped examples (src/genAutoExamplesWhitelist.sh) and check it in CI (§14.3 of the report).

summary: The whitelist that defines which contact models a binary supports is ignored by git through the style_* pattern, so it is not version-controlled. Make.sh uses it when it exists and otherwise generates all combinations. CMake ignores it and emits 4 combinations. The same commit can therefore give binaries with 4, 124 or about 1200 supported combinations.
failure_scenario: A fresh clone or a CI build produces a binary that supports different input decks from the developer's binary. Now that the fallback is gone, this appears as hard errors on decks that 'worked on my machine'.
recommendation: Track a canonical whitelist file under a non-ignored name, such as src/contact_model_whitelist.txt, and make both CMake and Make read it.

summary: The only regression deck cannot reach the error it is meant to test. (a) atom_style superquadric needs an ENABLE_SQ (Boost) build. (b) Its pair_style combination (HERTZ,TH,OFF,EPSD2,SUPERQUADRIC) is not whitelisted, so it stops at the whitelist error. (c) `set atom 1 type 2` leaves no type-1 atom, which gives 'Atom types must start from 1'. With (b) and (c) fixed in a copy, the expected error is produced.
failure_scenario: A CI job that greps for 'integration_scheme 4 requires' always fails, or passes on the wrong error if it only checks for a non-zero exit code. The negative test gives false confidence.
recommendation: Use a whitelisted combination, such as hooke/tangential history/surface superquadric, or whitelist the one the deck uses. Use type 1. Add a runner that checks for the exact expected message. Document that the test needs ENABLE_SQ.

summary: The superquadric tutorial uses (HERTZ,TH,OFF,EPSD2,SUPERQUADRIC). That combination is not in the curated whitelist, so the deck hard-errors even on an ENABLE_SQ build.
failure_scenario: Running the shipped superquadric example on an SQ build aborts at pair_style with the whitelist error.
recommendation: Add the combination to the whitelist. Include the superquadric decks in the example CI job for SQ builds.

summary: CMake writes generated headers (style_*.h, style_contact_model.h, version_liggghts.h) into the source directory. An out-of-tree build therefore changes src/: it overwrites the Makefile-generated whitelist, and concurrent build trees with different options race on the same files.
failure_scenario: Configuring build/ replaces the curated 124-entry src/style_contact_model.h with CMake's 4-entry list, so the next `make hdf5mpi` build silently loses combinations. The audit had to build from snapshot copies to avoid this.
recommendation: Generate these files into ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR} and add that directory to the include path.

summary: GET_SUBDIRS runs add_subdirectory on every subdirectory that has a CMakeLists.txt, including src/GPU_DEM. A CPU-only CMake configure therefore also configures the GPU scaffold. (The GPU code itself was not reviewed; it is out of scope.)
failure_scenario: A machine without a CUDA toolchain may fail or slow down the CPU configure because of an unrelated component. The audit excluded GPU_DEM by building from a snapshot copy.
recommendation: Put the GPU subproject behind an explicit option(ENABLE_GPU_DEM OFF).

summary: For GCC, CMake unconditionally adds `-O2 -ffast-math ...` to CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS, whatever the build type. The Makefile route (Makefile.mpi, Makefile.hdf5mpi) does not use -ffast-math. CMake and Make binaries therefore differ in floating-point semantics (no NaN/Inf handling, reassociation).
failure_scenario: A physics result or golden file made with one build route is not reproducible with the other. A NaN guard (x != x) may be optimized away in CMake builds.
recommendation: Remove -ffast-math from the defaults, or make it an option. The audit builds add -fno-fast-math.

summary: The CMake build has no HDF5 switch. dump hdf5 and dump mesh/hdf5 are compiled in only when -DLIGGGHTS_HDF5, the HDF5 include path and -lhdf5 are passed by hand. Only the Makefile route (Makefile.hdf5mpi) supports HDF5 out of the box.
failure_scenario: A CMake user runs in.chute_wear and gets 'Dump hdf5 requires a parallel HDF5 build', or at HEAD 'Invalid dump style'.
recommendation: Add option(ENABLE_HDF5) with find_package(HDF5 COMPONENTS C) and a check that HDF5_IS_PARALLEL is set.

summary: The version banner prints the HEAD commit with no dirty-tree marker. It lists the CMake ENABLE_MODEL_* set ('models: HERTZ ... ROLLING_EPSD2'), not the whitelist that was actually compiled. The modified binaries report the same commit as the baseline.
failure_scenario: Logs from the modified and pristine binaries cannot be told apart. The banner claims models that do not match the compiled whitelist.
recommendation: Use `git describe --dirty --always` and print the number of whitelisted combinations (or its hash).

summary: The LIGGGHTS_USE_SOA_NVE path exists only in FixNVE::initial_integrate/final_integrate. FixNVESphere, which every granular tutorial uses (19 nve/sphere, 0 plain nve), overrides both methods. No shipped granular deck can exercise the SoA code.
failure_scenario: Benchmarks of lmp_soa against lmp_release on the shipped decks measure nothing: the output is identical and the SoA code never runs. Any claimed SoA gain would be an artifact.
evidence_ref: audit/cases/smoke/*packing*/log.liggghts (identical thermo); grep of fix styles in examples
recommendation: Decide what §14.1 of the report asks: port the SoA path to nve/sphere, or delete it. Until then, any SoA benchmark must use `fix nve`.

summary: The Domain constructor calls set_lattice(), and the Lattice constructor then calls force->numeric() before LAMMPS::force has been created, which happens later at lammps.cpp:641. The member read is uninitialized. It works only because Force::numeric does not touch `this` on valid input.
failure_scenario: UBSan reports a misaligned member call on 0xbebebebe... at startup, on every run and every rank. With -fsanitize=vptr the process SEGVs before reading input. A different compiler or optimization level could crash here.
recommendation: Parse the default lattice value with atof/utils::numeric, not through `force`, or create Force before Domain. This is the same fix as upstream LAMMPS.

summary: generate_message() returns msg.c_str() of a local std::string, which is a dangling pointer. About 20% of the time Error::all/one then prints garbage after the ERROR line.
failure_scenario: Observed on the SQ build: after the whitelist error the output contains `dS'M-^\^E (…pair_gran_proxy.cpp:76)`. In the worst case this is an out-of-bounds read inside an error path.
recommendation: Return std::string by value or hold the message in a member.

summary: LeakSanitizer reports that mesh modules created by FixMeshSurface are never freed. The remaining leaks (about 11.5 KB in total) are inside OpenMPI.
failure_scenario: A one-off leak at shutdown. It does not affect results.
recommendation: Delete the mesh modules in the FixMeshSurface destructor.

summary: chute_wear gives different trajectories with 1 and 2 MPI ranks: particle 1 has z = 0.0478587 on 1 rank and 0.0523183 on 2 ranks at step 500, and there are 38 vs 37 atoms at step 3000. Baseline and modified builds behave identically, so this is legacy rank-count dependence in insertion, not a regression.
failure_scenario: Phase-2 cross-rank reproducibility tests on insertion-driven decks will fail regardless of the modifications and must use create_atoms/read_data initial states.
recommendation: Document this. Use a rank-independent initial configuration for V&V reproducibility cases.

summary: -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion at -O2 reports 15 warnings (matched line-insensitively) that are new relative to HEAD, and 2 that were removed: 14 -Wunused-parameter, 5 -Wshadow and 3 -Wconversion (size_t to int from strlen). None of them indicates a functional defect.
failure_scenario: No realistic failure. strlen of an input token above 2^31 is not reachable.
recommendation: Fix these in passing: cast strlen explicitly and mark unused parameters with /*name*/.

failure_scenario: It overflows only if one rank holds more than about 715 million selected atoms, which is unrealistic.

summary: The style-table key is std::pair<std::string,int>, but the contact-model hash is int64_t, so the hash is truncated when the key is built (legacy). Two combinations whose hashes differ only in the upper 32 bits would collide, and addStyle would print 'Style collision'.
failure_scenario: No collision is observed with the current 124 entries: no collision warning is printed. It could appear once more models are added.
recommendation: Use int64_t in the key type.
